title: Takaichi Rebuffs Trump's Push to Rename AI as "SI"
key_facts: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi was asked on 8 Oct 2026 in the House of Representatives about renaming artificial intelligence 'superintelligence' (SI), Kyodo News reported.
The question came from Yuichiro Tamaki, leader of the Democratic Party for the People.
Takaichi said AI is the right term at this stage, that it is used universally including in government documents and academic papers, and that replacing it everywhere immediately would be difficult.
She said she would watch how the international community and other governments respond.
Trump called for SI instead of AI in his UN General Assembly keynote last month and said the US federal government would replace AI with SI in official documents.
Takaichi has stressed her personal rapport with Trump; he called her a 'wonderful friend and partner' at a March summit.
quote_evidence: Takaichi expressed a negative view of the proposal to call AI "superintelligence," or SI, during questioning in the House of Representatives on the 8th, Kyodo News reported.
She stressed that the term AI is used universally, including in government documents and academic papers, and that replacing it everywhere immediately would be difficult.
He said the U.S. federal government would replace AI with SI in official documents and expressed hope that the rest of the world would follow his change in terminology.
why_it_matters_hint: Shows a close US ally declining to follow the US president's call to rename AI.
notes: Seoul Economic Daily article is AI-translated from Korean and says quotes may not match the original wording; it credits Kyodo News for the parliamentary exchange. Continues C05-02 (Trump's Truth Social post of 8 Oct 2026).
